correctness.rationale: Every stability inequality is obtained by exact directed one-agent comparisons; mixed-coalition necessity and singleton cases are addressed. Cauchy–Schwarz identifies the unrestricted optimum and equality. Integral residuals force equal ratios for divisible populations, while explicit (1,q) / (1,q+1) blocks prove the sharp converse and positive exact gap. The weak blocking coalition and labeled enumeration are proved. A separate exact-arithmetic script tests 684404 labeled partitions across 25 parameter pairs and independently reproduces all 5155 Nash incidences, but the infinite theorem relies on symbolic proof, not the finite test.

evidence: Bilò et al., JAIR 62 (2018), pp. 338-340, Lemma 12, give a welfare-merging inequality for two complete bipartite subcoalitions with equality at equal ratios.
The same article derives general unweighted-bipartite price-of-stability bounds and examples of noncomplete bipartite graphs, not an all-Nash-states characterization on the complete bipartite family.
Brandl, Brandt and Strobel, AAMAS 2015, abstract, give general impossibility and computational complexity, without a stated complete-bipartite arithmetic classification; only abstract inspected.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general result that all optimal blocks share a type ratio does not imply all individually stable partitions have that ratio. The missing implication is proved by the new integer-residual Nash argument; a converse explicit Nash witness covers nondivisibility. Broader bipartite topology bounds address best equilibrium welfare, not whether every Nash state coincides with an optimal strict-core partition.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known ratio-based strict core and welfare optimality statements are explicitly credited as prior work. Neither alone nor jointly proves every Nash equilibrium is proportional in divisible instances, since Nash moves are unilateral and may permit other partitions. The determinant interval plus integral sign separation establishes that implication; its nondivisible converse and exact Nash enumeration are likewise not implications of the cited group-stability and welfare identities.

The new one-player Nash determinant spectrum, arithmetic all-equilibria coincidence boundary, counterexamples and labeled Nash count are not stated in the primary material inspected nor implied by its group-stability or welfare statements. residual_risks: Neither specialist literature coverage nor global priority can be proven from database search nonmatches.

The short 2014 WINE Nash-stability predecessor was located bibliographically but not read in full; its 2018 expanded same-author article was inspected for the specific model and welfare lemma.

value.rationale: Two-type complete bipartite FHGs form a canonical coalition-composition model; the theorem determines the exact condition under which individually stable outcomes cannot be inefficient or leave the strict core. This is an all-size structural boundary with a complete finite test for arbitrary proposed partitions, exact divisible-case labeled enumeration, and quantitative genuinely inefficient Nash witnesses outside the boundary. It addresses a meaningful stability/efficiency gap and is not a mere parameter substitution or small numerical table.
